primary_audit.summary: Mostly faithful adventure with strong beats. Defects center on the confusing rope and rescue mechanics, glider and line continuity, some geography and time inconsistencies, and a few awkward phrasings.

findings.exact_text: arriving at his shoulder
findings.reason: This compressed body-position phrase is unnatural; English ordinarily places someone “at his side” or “beside him.”

findings.exact_text: something she wished she didn't want
findings.reason: The nested verbs create an unclear, unnatural expression of reluctant agreement.

findings.exact_text: a slope of tangle
findings.reason: “Tangle” is not naturally used as a mass noun in this construction; “a tangled slope” conveys the image clearly.

findings.exact_text: flattened every tree inland into a lean
findings.reason: “Into a lean” is an unnatural result phrase for trees bent persistently by wind.

findings.exact_text: Around the trunk, half-sunk into bark that had grown over it, ran a length
findings.reason: The extended inverted construction delays the subject and makes the physical image unnecessarily difficult to parse.

findings.exact_text: dropped away to cloud sea
findings.reason: The established geographical noun phrase requires the article: “the cloud sea.”

findings.exact_text: a cliff overlook gave him the whole interior at a glance
findings.reason: “Cliff overlook” and “gave him the whole interior” form strained collocations that obscure the otherwise simple viewpoint description.

findings.exact_text: the same corridor we arrived
findings.reason: “Arrived” cannot directly take “corridor” as its object; the sentence needs a preposition such as “through.”

findings.exact_text: half-hidden by fern
findings.reason: For ordinary visible vegetation, English naturally uses “ferns” or “a fern,” not singular bare “fern.”

findings.exact_text: reading the exact same moment he did
findings.reason: A person can read a situation or intention, but “read a moment” is an unnatural and unclear collocation here.

findings.exact_text: the old knot-trunk
findings.reason: The improvised compound “knot-trunk” is unnecessarily compressed and briefly ambiguous.

findings.exact_text: laughed until she had to stop
findings.reason: This is tautological and vague; specifying that she ran out of breath gives the phrase a natural endpoint.

language_sentence_scan.rewrite: "I saw it first," Nisa said, arriving at his side.
Then at him, and her jaw set in the particular way it did when she was about to agree with something she wished she didn't.
It was a tangled slope—a hillside of old roots spilled over the island's edge like the fingers of something buried.
Wind had bent every tree inland at an angle, as if the whole forest had spent centuries flinching from one direction.
A length of bleached rope fiber ran around the trunk, half-sunk into bark that had grown over it, knotted in a hitch he almost recognized—a guild-style anchor, but not any pattern currently taught.
Bridges made of living root spanned gaps that dropped away to the cloud sea, grown in arcs no carpenter could copy.
On the far side of the bridge, an overlook at the cliff's edge gave him a view of the whole interior, and what he saw stopped him cold: the old knots didn't stop.
Then the final pages: *We depart by the same corridor we arrived through.
At the camp's far edge, half-hidden by ferns, a carved wind-vane pointed deeper inland—and beyond it, visible through a break in the trees, stood a shape on the high ground.

The bridge fell away beneath him into the cloud sea, taking the rope's last anchor with it, and Arda swung free on the cut length still gripped in his fist, and Nisa—reading the situation at exactly the same moment he did—leaned back and hauled, and his hand found her wrist, and her grip found him, and that was what saved him.
The glider still held where the trunk with the old knot leaned.
Nisa sat down on the wooden rail and laughed until she ran out of breath.

secondary_audit.summary: The story is highly fluent overall. Twelve sentences need local wording repairs for compressed spatial phrasing, strained collocations, missing grammar, or immediate clarity.
